title: Cycles and inversions
key_idea: Every permutation decomposes uniquely into **cycles**. The **signless Stirling number** $c(n,k) = \left[\begin{smallmatrix}n\\k\end{smallmatrix}\right]$ counts permutations of $[n]$ with exactly $k$ cycles. Their OGF is $\sum_k c(n,k) x^k = x(x+1)(x+2)\cdots(x+n-1)$ (rising factorial). **Inversions**: $(i,j)$ with $i<j$ but $w(i)>w(j)$; tracked by $\text{inv}(w)$, the $q$-weight $\sum_w q^{\text{inv}(w)} = [n]_q!$.
summary: **To be filled in when you reach this section.** Topics: cycle notation, the cycle lemma, signless Stirling numbers $c(n,k)$ and their recurrence $c(n,k) = c(n-1,k-1) + (n-1)c(n-1,k)$, inversion tables, the bijection between inversion tables and permutations, and the $q$-analogue $[n]_q! = \sum_w q^{\text{inv}(w)}$.

notation.description: Signless Stirling number of the first kind: number of $w \in S_n$ with exactly $k$ cycles
Number of inversions of $w$: $|\{(i,j): i<j, w(i)>w(j)\}|$
